record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: What is the minimum number of steps of square completion needed to obtain a word from one of its factors?

evidence.quote: What is the minimum number of steps of square completion needed to obtain a word from one of its factors?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. For a word $w \in \Sigma^*$, a prefix-suffix square completion step transforms $w$ either into $w \cdot s$, where $s$ is a nonempty suffix of $w$ (so the result has $ss$ as a suffix), or into $p \cdot w$, where $p$ is a nonempty prefix of $w$ (so the result has $pp$ as a prefix). Given a word $u \in \Sigma^*$ and a factor (contiguous subword) $v$ of $u$, suppose there exists a sequence of prefix-suffix square completion steps starting from $v$ and ending at $u$. Define $f(u,v)$ to be the minimum length of such a sequence, and let $F(u) = \min_{v} f(u,v)$, where the minimum runs over all proper factors $v$ of $u$ from which $u$ can be reached by such steps. Determine $F(u)$ as a function of $u$ (in particular, give tight upper and lower bounds on the minimum number of prefix-suffix square completion steps needed to obtain a word from one of its factors).
artifact.status_search_result: Web search confirms prefix-suffix square completion is a studied operation in combinatorics on words, with a known linear-time procedure for deciding generability and results on iterated completion generating infinite words. However, no source found explicitly resolves the minimum number of square completion steps required to reach a word from one of its factors, so the status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: Prefix-Suffix Square Completion
status_evidence.snippet: linear time procedure that, given two words, decides whether the longer can be generated by iterated prefix-suffix square completion from the shorter
status_evidence.claim: Decision problem for prefix-suffix square completion is solved in linear time, but the minimum-step optimization is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Square Completion Operation of Maximal Suffix in Fibonacci Word
status_evidence.snippet: strict square completion of maximal suffix... can be used iteratively to generate the Fibonacci word
status_evidence.claim: Related square completion variants are studied, but the specific minimum-steps question is not resolved here.
